title: Eleven Chairs in a Barn
subtitle: 戏剧表演 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 戏剧表演（文学艺术与体育·戏剧与表演）
meta: 主题语境：戏剧表演（文学艺术与体育·戏剧与表演）　|　核心词汇：comedy　|　正文 342 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 comedy 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1958 my uncle ① staged a comedy in a barn with eleven chairs, and he said the staging was the whole of the rehearsal. The ② comedy, meaning the play and not the barn, ran eleven minutes too long and stayed that way; comedy, he said, is the only thing in a barn that is judged by how many chairs are filled.

Every ③ comedy in that company had the same eleven chairs, and the ④ comedy at the end, meaning the one he kept for the harvest and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever asked for twice. Comedy, my aunt said, is nine parts timing and one part somebody willing to fall over; my uncle said the timing is the part that fills the barn.

My mother meant the other thing entirely: she said ⑤ the comedy of the whole afternoon was the whole of the afternoon, meaning the mistakes and not the play. The ⑥ comedy, meaning the mistakes and not any of that, is the only thing in an afternoon that everybody laughs at and nobody planned; comedy, she said, is either something you stage or the only word that means both a play and a set of mistakes. He said the mistakes are the part they remember.

By 1967 the ⑦ comedy had become a line in a review, and the review had become an argument about the chairs. The ⑧ comedy of the whole thing, my uncle wrote in July, was one barn and forty years of falling over; comedy, he said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to keep the chairs. She said the chairs were never mentioned.

The ⑨ comedy I remember is the one at the end, which was staged in 1973 and is still described as the loudest in the county. A ⑩ comedy, my aunt said in 1975, is the only thing that improves by being laughed at; every comedy, she said, is a mistake that has agreed to look like a play. She said the mistake was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: B. n. 喜剧（指那一出戏本身，与那个谷仓相对）
C. 固定搭配：stage a comedy 上演一出喜剧
D. n. 喜剧（指那个剧团里每一出）
E. n. 喜剧（指末尾那一出）
F. n. 滑稽；喜剧性（抽象：那些差错带来的滑稽）
G. n. 喜剧（指评论里提到的那一出）
H. n. 圆满的收场（抽象总称，喜剧式结局）

items.q: staged a comedy in a barn with eleven chairs
The comedy, meaning the play and not the barn
the comedy of the whole afternoon was the whole of the afternoon

answers.why: stage a comedy 意为“上演一出喜剧”，1958 年叔叔在一个只有十一把椅子的谷仓里上演了一出喜剧。
comedy 意为“喜剧”，指那一出戏本身而不是那个谷仓，它演得长了十一分钟。
comedy 指那个剧团里每一出喜剧，每一出都用同样的十一把椅子。
comedy 指末尾那一出（他留给丰收节的那一出），是唯一有人要过两次的。
comedy 意为“滑稽、喜剧性”，母亲说整个下午的滑稽就是那个下午的全部，指的是那些差错。
comedy 为抽象用法，指那些差错而不是那出戏，是下午里人人都笑、却无人预谋的东西。
comedy 意为“喜剧”，指评论里提到的那一出，到 1967 年这出喜剧成了评论里的一行。
comedy 意为“圆满的收场”，叔叔七月写道，整件事的收场是一个谷仓四十年的摔倒。
comedy 意为“喜剧”，我记得的是末尾那一出，1973 年上演，至今仍被说成全县最热闹的。
comedy 为抽象总称，姑姑说一出喜剧是唯一会因为被笑而变好的东西。
